symbols.name: V
symbols.type: A finite nonempty set of observed vertices
symbols.role: Observed variables.

symbols.name: U
symbols.type: A finite set of mutually independent exogenous root vertices
symbols.role: Latent sources.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.type: The input family \(\Omega=(\Omega_i:i\in V)\) of specified finite nonempty observed alphabets
symbols.role: Observed state spaces supplied explicitly to the decision problem; finite latent alphabets are part of a witness model and must be bounded by the latent-lifting result.

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: A finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup U\) in which every vertex in \(U\) is a root
symbols.role: The latent-variable causal graph.

symbols.name: W
symbols.type: A subset \(W\subseteq V\)
symbols.role: Observed nodes known to be deterministic functions of their parents, without their functions being known.

symbols.name: Pi
symbols.type: A finite conjunction \(\Pi\) of literals \(P(A=a)>0\) or \(P(A=a)=0\), where \(A\subseteq V\)
symbols.role: Declared observational support information.

symbols.name: X
symbols.type: A subset \(X\subseteq V\)
symbols.role: Treatment vertices.

symbols.name: CV
symbols.type: The Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\)
symbols.role: Comparator-specific positivity premise, distinct from the declared support-literal input \(\Pi\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.type: A subset \(Y\subseteq V\setminus X\)
symbols.role: Outcome vertices.

symbols.name: x
symbols.type: An assignment \(x\in\prod_{i\in X}\Omega_i\)
symbols.role: Fixed intervention value.

symbols.name: y
symbols.type: An assignment \(y\in\prod_{i\in Y}\Omega_i\)
symbols.role: Fixed outcome event.

symbols.name: M
symbols.type: A finite causal Bayesian-network model on \(G\) whose observed variables have alphabets \(\Omega\) and whose latent roots have finite model-specific alphabets
symbols.role: A generic model with mutually independent root laws and finite conditional probability tables; the tables at \(W\) are deterministic.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.type: The observed law \(P_M(V)\)
symbols.role: The observational input to any returned formula.

symbols.name: Pint
symbols.type: The postintervention law \(P_{M,x}\) obtained by replacing the structural equations at \(X\) by \(x\)
symbols.role: Interventional distribution.

symbols.name: q
symbols.type: The scalar query \(q(M)=P_{M,x}(Y=y)\)
symbols.role: Target causal event probability.

symbols.name: S
symbols.type: A subset \(S\subseteq\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i\)
symbols.role: A candidate exact observed support.

symbols.name: ModelClass
symbols.type: The class \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\)
symbols.role: Compatible finite independent-root SCMs.

symbols.name: GuardedFormula
symbols.type: A finite support-guarded expression \(F(P_M(V))\)
symbols.role: A formula using finite sums, products, and ratios only on branches certifying positive denominators.

symbols.name: TraceGrammar
symbols.type: A finite labelled partial-trace grammar \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\)
symbols.role: The proposed obstruction language retaining ancestral and district provenance, reached response rows, support guards, and functional-row quotient labels.

symbols.name: Certificate
symbols.type: A finite terminal certificate \(C\) emitted by a derivation in \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}\)
symbols.role: Either a support contradiction, a guarded formula derivation, or a NONID certificate containing two fully encoded rational witness models.

symbols.name: InputSize
symbols.type: The integer \(L=L(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) equal to the bit length of the finite encoded input
symbols.role: Size parameter for search and arithmetic certificate bounds.

symbols.name: CertificateLength
symbols.type: The bit length \(\ell(C)\) of an encoded terminal certificate \(C\)
symbols.role: Certificate-size parameter for the rule-checking and output-size bounds to be derived by the latent-lifting open question.

symbols.name: LatentCardinalityBound
symbols.type: A positive integer-valued bound \(H(L)\) to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:latent-lifting}\)
symbols.role: Maximum model-specific alphabet cardinality needed for each root vertex \(u\in U\) in a returned NONID witness.

symbols.name: PrimitiveBitBound
symbols.type: A positive integer-valued bound \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\) to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:latent-lifting}\)
symbols.role: Maximum binary length of each separately reduced numerator-denominator pair in a rational NONID certificate.

symbols.name: FIDS
symbols.type: A three-output procedure \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\)
symbols.role: The target graph-and-support decision algorithm.

symbols.name: StrictPattern
symbols.type: The binary latent functional supported-bow instance \(\mathcal B_0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:first-strict-pattern}\)
symbols.role: The first explicit input on which support-sensitive state-specific resolution lies outside ordinary ID, is not resolved by Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, violates the Theorem 18 treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\), and lies outside Chen--Darwiche's 2026 strictly-positive CSI and state-alphabet setup.

assumptions.condition: The exogenous law factorizes as \(P_M(U)=\prod_{u\in U}P_M(u)\).
For every \(w\in W\), the conditional mechanism at \(w\) is a point mass for every joint value of its observed and latent parents.
The observed law satisfies every literal in \(\Pi\), written \(P_M(V)\models\Pi\).

novel.justification: Declared positive and structural-zero events are auditable inputs in finite systems with protocol-impossible states, deterministic routing, or registry-enforced exclusions. This input may contain arbitrary marginal or joint zeros; it is distinct from Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15's separability and parent conditions and from Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\).

definitions.name: Functional-support SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)=\{M:M\text{ is a finite causal Bayesian-network model on }G,\ M\text{ assigns alphabet }\Omega_i\text{ to every }i\in V\text{ and a finite alphabet to every }u\in U,\ P_M(U)=\prod_{u\in U}P_M(u),\ M\text{ obeys the qualitative functional restrictions on }W,\ P_M(V)\models\Pi\}\).

definitions.name: Support-valid guarded formula
definitions.construction: A finite family \(F=(F_S:S\subseteq\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i)\) in which each \(F_S\) is an observed-cell expression formed by finite sums, products, and ratios, and every denominator used by \(F_S\) is certified positive by the guard \(\operatorname{supp}(P_M(V))=S\); evaluation returns \(F_{\operatorname{supp}(P_M(V))}(P_M(V))\).

definitions.name: Fully observed completion obstruction
definitions.construction: When \(U=\varnothing\), for an exact support \(S\), record two deterministic completions \(h,h'\) of all parent rows not reached by \(S\), sharing every reached row and every restriction at \(W\), such that \(\mathbf 1\{Y_x(h)=y\}\ne\mathbf 1\{Y_x(h')=y\}\).

definitions.name: Functional-support trace-grammar handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}\) by adapting recursive ancestral restriction and district decomposition while retaining every partial deletion trace; label each trace by its reachable observed support relation, its equality classes of functional response rows, and the exact residual query; terminal failures are converted into bounded forest-supported response obstructions rather than being declared by semantic nonidentifiability.

definitions.name: Latent-source architecture of \(G\)
definitions.construction: A witness model \(M_j\) preserves the latent-source architecture of \(G\) when it uses exactly the root vertices \(U\) with precisely the parent incidences specified by \(G\), assigns each \(u\in U\) a finite model-specific latent alphabet of size at most \(H(L)\), and satisfies \(P_{M_j}(U)=\prod_{u\in U}P_{M_j}(u)\). No latent source is merged or added and no cross-source dependence is introduced. The two witness models may assign different marginal masses to the same root vertex; no latent-root law is part of the input.

definitions.name: \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}\) construction handle
definitions.construction: Design \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) by enumerating only support worlds over the supplied observed product alphabet \(\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i\), then running support-guarded ancestral and district reductions over \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}\), and finally lifting every terminal response obstruction source by source while preserving \(\Omega\), exact support, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:latent-source-architecture}\).

definitions.name: Rational NONID certificate encoding
definitions.construction: For each returned model \(M_j\), serialize every primitive latent-root mass \(\lambda^{(j)}_{u,r}=P_{M_j}(u=r)\) and every primitive observed-node table entry \(\theta^{(j)}_{i,b\mid a}=P_{M_j}(i=b\mid\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)\) as its own coprime pair of nonnegative integers \((p,d)\) with \(d\ge 1\); no common denominator is required. The sum of the numerator and denominator binary lengths of every pair is at most \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\), and every latent-root alphabet has size at most \(H(L)\). Each induced observed or interventional cell is encoded by its exact finite sum-product circuit over these pairs together with its reduced output pair. Writing \(K_V=\prod_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), every reduced cell pair has binary length at most \(H(L)^{|U|}((|V|+|U|)B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)+|U|\lceil\log_2 H(L)\rceil+1)\), and the complete two-model certificate has serialized bit length at most \(8(L+1)K_VH(L)^{2|U|}(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)+\lceil\log_2 H(L)\rceil+L+1)\).

definitions.name: First strict latent support pattern
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal B_0\) have binary observed nodes \(A,D,B\), one binary latent root \(H\), arrows \(H\to A\), \(H\to B\), \(A\to D\), \(A\to B\), and \(D\to B\), observed alphabets \(\Omega_A=\Omega_D=\Omega_B=\{0,1\}\), the qualitative functional declaration \(W=\{D\}\), and the single support literal \(P(A=1)=0\). Consider the two state-specific queries \(P_{A=0}(B=b)\) and \(P_{A=1}(B=b)\), for \(b\in\{0,1\}\).

definitions.name: Independent-root kill instance
definitions.construction: Take binary roots \(U_1,U_2\), binary observed nodes \(A,B,C\), and arrows \(U_1\to A,B\), \(U_2\to A,C\), \(A\to B\), and \(B\to C\); enumerate its \(2^{12}=4096\) deterministic response skeletons, all exact observed supports of size at most four, and the queries \(P_{A=a}(C=c)\).

statements.statement: For every fixed finite response skeleton over the supplied observed alphabets \(\Omega\), consistency of \(\Pi\) and every support entailment are decidable by finite possible-world relation enumeration. Every feasible single-model support stratum contains a rational independent-root model obtained by assigning uniform mass on each selected primitive root or table-row support; each primitive probability is stored as a separate reduced fraction with denominator at most the size of that support, and no common denominator is asserted.
statements.justification: This separates genuine inconsistency from identification and supplies the finite support front end.
statements.gap: Fraser proves possibilistic compatibility by possible worlds, but does not impose named functional nodes while retaining a causal query and an independent-root probabilistic realization.
statements.consumer: A support-aware causal-analysis backend can reject contradictory structural-zero and functional declarations before attempting effect identification.

statements.statement: If \(U=\varnothing\) and \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\ne\varnothing\), then \(q\) is identified if and only if no exact support \(S\) realized by a member of \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) admits a fully observed completion obstruction. Agreement yields a support-valid guarded g-formula. Disagreement yields an existentially constructed pair of compatible rational models \(M_1,M_2\) with the same observed law and exact support and with instance-dependent target gap \(\Delta=|q(M_1)-q(M_2)|>0\). For this constructed pair, every primitive observed-node conditional-table probability is encoded as its own reduced fraction with denominator at most \(8|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\) and pair length at most \(2\lceil\log_2(8|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|)\rceil+2\) bits; no common denominator is required, and induced cells are exact sum-product evaluations of those fractions.
statements.justification: This is the exact causally sufficient base case and fixes the support and arithmetic invariants that any latent lifting theorem must preserve.
statements.gap: Classical g-formula arguments assume access to the needed rows, whereas functional elimination results do not give this row-completion equivalence under arbitrary support literals.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives a complete structural-zero decision rule for causally sufficient discrete Bayesian networks and a regression test for the latent algorithm.

statements.statement: Can the partial-trace handle be completed into a bounded finite-production grammar \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}\) such that every residual failure contains a forest-supported local response obstruction that extends to two models \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) satisfying \(P_{M_1}(V)=P_{M_2}(V)\), \(\operatorname{supp}_V(M_1)=\operatorname{supp}_V(M_2)\), and witness-dependent target separation \(\Delta=|q(M_1)-q(M_2)|>0\), while preserving the supplied observed alphabets \(\Omega\) and the latent-source architecture of \(G\): each \(M_j\) uses exactly the roots \(U\) with the parent incidences of \(G\), may use finite model-specific latent alphabets bounded by \(H(L)\), and separately satisfies \(P_{M_j}(U)=\prod_{u\in U}P_{M_j}(u)\), without requiring \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) to share root masses? Can absence of an obstruction reconstruct a support-valid guarded formula, and can exhaustive search of the grammar terminate within an explicit bound and return exactly one terminal certificate on every input: a support contradiction when \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)=\varnothing\), and otherwise either a guarded formula derivation or a NONID certificate? The grammar must specify the finite syntax of each terminal certificate. Conditional on that completed syntax and rule set, it must make rule recognition decidable: support contradictions are checked by finite support enumeration; guarded derivations are checked production by production with every positivity guard and compiled to an observable expression; and NONID certificates are checked by exact rational arithmetic for normalization, graph and functional-row compatibility, satisfaction of \(\Pi\), equality of all observed cells and exact support, unequal targets, preservation of the latent-source architecture, and the encoding bounds in \(\mathrm{def:rational-certificate-encoding}\). The result must derive explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\), an explicit search-state bound in \(L\), and explicit computable bit-operation and output-size bounds in \(L\) and \(\ell(C)\) for checking a supplied terminal certificate. It must resolve \(\mathcal B_0\), strictly extend ordinary hedge completeness, go beyond Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions, and admit declared support faces outside the Theorem 18 treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). It must also strictly cover the residual regime outside Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2: arbitrary declared zero-and-positive event literals and qualitative functional nodes, rather than only their sound identification under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law. For each existentially constructed rational witness pair, every rational pair must use the primitive, individual-denominator encoding of \(\mathrm{def:rational-certificate-encoding}\), including its displayed induced-cell and total serialized bit-size bounds; no instance-uniform lower bound on \(\Delta\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it must replace classical parity softening by an exact support-preserving lift that retains the latent-source architecture of \(G\).
statements.gap: Shpitser and Pearl construct unrestricted binary hedge pairs. Chen and Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions, whereas Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem takes arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support literals as input. Chen and Darwiche's constrained-identifiability work gives arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests, including logical and \(0\)--\(1\) constraints, but not a complete procedure for this arbitrary support-literal and functional class or an exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy. Chen and Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 prove soundness of formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints, under a strictly positive observational law; they neither prove completeness under those constraints nor admit an input that keeps a treatment state in \(\Omega\) while declaring its observational probability zero. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash give a sound-and-complete gID algorithm under a positive observational law, but do not handle arbitrary declared support faces or supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe bound source cardinality. None proves the required exact-support rational pair or its converse formula reconstruction.
statements.consumer: Resolving the question turns qualitative mechanism and support knowledge into auditable identification or nonidentification certificates for latent causal graphs.

statements.statement: When \(W=\varnothing\) and \(\Pi\) entails strict positivity of every observed cell over \(\prod_{i\in V}\Omega_i\), \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) reduces to ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\): its successful expression agrees with the ordinary ID functional and every failure trace contains a corrected query-specific hedge.
statements.justification: This is the mandatory sanity reduction and rules out an unrelated support calculus masquerading as causal identification.
statements.gap: The correction in Shpitser's failure characterization makes the hedge query-specific; the reduction must preserve that corrected scope.
statements.consumer: Existing users obtain the same answer as ordinary ID whenever no new functional or support information is supplied.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal B_0\), \(P_{A=0}(B=b)=P(B=b)\) for every compatible model, whereas \(P_{A=1}(B=1)\) is not identified. For the latter claim, take \(H\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), set \(A=0\), let the functional node satisfy \(D=A\), and set \(B=H\) on the reached row \((A,D)=(0,0)\) in both models; on the intervention-exposed row \((A,D)=(1,1)\), set \(B=0\) in the first model and \(B=1\) in the second. The models have the identical exact-support observed law \(P(A=0,D=0,B=b)=1/2\) and respective targets zero and one. Ordinary ID fails for the latent bow remaining after accounting for the directed paths. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination, under its stated separability and parent conditions, leaves that unidentified bow, while Theorem 18 is inapplicable because its treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\) includes \(\Pr(A=1)>0\), which the declared support contradicts. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 prove soundness only for formula-returning algorithms under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law; \(\mathcal B_0\) instead retains \(1\in\Omega_A\) as a valid intervention state while declaring \(P(A=1)=0\), so it is outside their input regime. Thus this exact functional-support pattern is strictly resolved by the proposed support trichotomy on a residual regime not covered by those comparators.
statements.justification: The pattern exposes, on the smallest latent bow, both the supported state-specific formula branch and an exact-support rational NONID branch.
statements.gap: Ordinary ID gives only bow failure. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 elimination of \(D\), under its separability and parent conditions, leaves the bow, and Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem separates the supported and unsupported intervention values on this declared structural-zero face. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound identification results for CSI and state-alphabet constraints under strict observational positivity, not a completeness or exact-support countermodel result for a valid treatment state assigned zero observational mass.
statements.consumer: The pattern is a unit test requiring a support-aware implementation to return \(P(B=b)\) for \(A=0\) and an exact two-model certificate for \(A=1\).

statements.statement: Can each candidate finite grammar produced while resolving the latent-lifting question pass the following bounded computational validation target on the binary independent-root kill instance: enumerate all \(4096\) deterministic response skeletons, every exact observed support of size at most four, and every query \(P_{A=a}(C=c)\); compare each candidate formula classification with constancy on the corresponding observational fiber; and compare each candidate obstruction with an explicit pair of full models having equal observed laws, the same exact support, unequal targets, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\)? Any candidate grammar failing one comparison is rejected.
statements.justification: This finite computation is a falsifiable validation gate for architecture-preserving extension before a general grammar is accepted.
statements.gap: No cited completeness proof checks simultaneous preservation of two independent sources, an exact structural-zero face, and a state-specific intervention on this graph.
statements.consumer: The bounded audit rejects a candidate obstruction production before it is used in the general completeness proof or implementation.

sampling_model.design: Population-level finite SCM identification from the full observed law with \(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y\) supplied to the decision problem; no experimental randomization is assumed.
sampling_model.units: The identification statements compare all finite SCMs inducing the same observed distribution; sampling enters only after identification.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention replaces the equations at \(X\) by the fixed assignment \(x\).
sampling_model.overlap: The novel input \(\Pi\) declares arbitrary positive or zero observed events. It is distinct from Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15's separability and parent conditions and from Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); only denominators executed on a support branch must be certified positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the kernel; a multinomial plug-in estimator is available after a guarded formula is returned.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The ID algorithm is sound and complete for ordinary latent causal effect identification.

Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions; Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\).
Arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests address constrained identifiability, including logical and \(0\)--\(1\) constraints.

Theorems 1--2 prove soundness of formula-returning algorithms for state-based causal effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints; the paper assumes a strictly positive observational distribution and does not claim completeness under those constraints.
A formula may require positivity only for the events introduced in its derivation.
Theorem 5 makes Algorithm 1 terminating and sound, while Theorem 6 shows that identification in every context-specific DAG need not imply identification from the observed law.
Completeness holds for context-specific independences controlled by observed root variables.
The gID algorithm is sound and complete under positivity of the observational distribution.
Possible-world diagrams give a complete solution to possibilistic causal compatibility.
Finite latent cardinality bounds can preserve multiple independent sources.
Canonical finite response types reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs.

tldr: The paper asks for a complete support-aware analogue of the ID algorithm, \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\), for finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events. Its bounded partial-trace grammar must either refute the declarations, derive a guarded formula for \(P_x(y)\), or lift a local obstruction to two exact-support rational SCMs with the same observed law while preserving \(\Omega\) and the latent-source architecture of \(G\): exactly the root vertices and parent incidences of \(G\), model-specific finite latent alphabets, and sourcewise independence in each model, without shared root masses across the pair. Each existentially constructed rational witness uses individually reduced primitive root and conditional-table fractions, not an unspecified common denominator, with derived latent-cardinality and serialized bit bounds, and has a witness-dependent target separation \(\Delta>0\) rather than an absolute gap guarantee. Finite terminal-certificate syntax, decidable rule checking, and explicit checker and search bounds are obligations of the open grammar construction. The supported-bow pattern \(\mathcal B_0\) is the first explicit case beyond ordinary ID, Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). It also lies outside Chen--Darwiche's 2026 sound state-based algorithms, whose inputs are context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints under a strictly positive observational law, because \(\mathcal B_0\) retains intervention state \(A=1\) in \(\Omega_A\) while declaring \(P(A=1)=0\). The declared support-literal regime is likewise outside the positive-observational-law scope of the sound-and-complete gID result of Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash. The genuinely open content is exhaustive search termination, finite grammar and certificate construction, the general latent lift, converse formula reconstruction, and associated complexity bounds.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary hedge completeness ignores declared structural-zero faces. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under stated separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not a complete formula-or-exact-support-countermodel procedure for valid intervention states on structural-zero faces. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete gID under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces, and do not supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Tikka--Hyttinen--Karvanen Theorem 5 supplies a terminating sound CSI search, and Theorem 6 shows why contextwise answers do not give completeness.
project_justification.niche: Finite categorical latent SCMs with explicit observed alphabets admit combinatorial support certificates and canonical response coordinates, but existing tools do not coordinate them with query-specific hedge traces, exact witness lifting that preserves the latent-source architecture of \(G\), and auditable rational serialization.
project_justification.fill: A terminating \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) procedure will preserve \(\Omega\), support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) through recursion and certify every terminal outcome with a guarded formula, a contradiction, or a rational separating pair obeying explicit primitive and total bit bounds. The grammar construction must also provide finite certificate syntax, decidable rule checking, and explicit checker and search complexity bounds.

related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply recursive district decomposition and classical parity hedge pairs; the present kernel requires every pair to preserve the declared exact support, supplied observed alphabets, fixed functional rows, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\), with no shared root-mass requirement. Shpitser's correction ties an obstruction to the actual failed query. Chen and Darwiche's Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions. Their Theorem 18 instead assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). Neither theorem identifies the declared support-literal regime \(\Pi\), a new input here that may include arbitrary marginal or joint zeros. technical_internal_limitation: The fully observed completion argument does not survive marginalization: equality of observed laws becomes a system of polynomial equalities in products of latent-source probabilities, so a local target-varying direction need not factor into independent sources. A real separating fiber also need not contain a rational point. These are the two obligations of Open-ended Question 1, not assumptions of the proposal.
honest_scope: The finite support oracle, supported-bow separation, and fully observed completion frontier are derived but remain to be independently proved. Exhaustive search termination, the finite latent obstruction grammar and terminal-certificate syntax, decidable checking with explicit checker and search bounds, extension preserving the latent-source architecture of \(G\), converse formula reconstruction, existence of rational separating pairs in the stated individual-fraction encoding, and explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\) are open. A separating witness must have \(\Delta>0\), but the gap may depend on the obstructed instance and witness; no absolute gap constant is claimed. Generic real quantifier elimination, unrestricted latent flattening, and the fully observed special case do not count as resolutions of the latent headline.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level results are Shpitser--Pearl hedge completeness and Chen--Darwiche's 2024 and 2026 results. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, while Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen and Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 establish soundness of formula-returning state-based algorithms under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not completeness under those constraints or an exact-support paired-witness trichotomy. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash establish sound-and-complete gID for positive observational laws, but neither arbitrary declared support faces nor exact-support rational paired witnesses are part of that result. The explicit latent bow \(\mathcal B_0\) is resolved state by state even though ordinary ID fails, Theorem 15 elimination leaves the bow, Theorem 18's premise is false because \(\Pr(A=1)=0\), and the 2026 input regime excludes the face because \(A=1\) remains a valid state in \(\Omega_A\) but has zero observational probability. The general kernel changes the load-bearing witness step: every terminal obstruction must extend through discarded districts to two full models with the latent-source architecture of \(G\), supplied observed alphabets, named functional rows, identical exact observed support, and individually encoded rational primitives satisfying a total serialized bit bound. Each model uses exactly the root vertices and parent incidences of \(G\), has its own finite latent alphabets and product root law, and need not share root masses with the other witness. Each constructed pair need only have witness-dependent separation \(\Delta>0\). Conversely, absence of an obstruction must reconstruct a guarded observable formula. None of the named comparators proves either direction on this arbitrary declared-support domain.
